basis: Combined factor IX and XI deficiency is a coagulation disorder; bleeding does not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Acute inflammation of the Eustachian tube; the concept does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Essential hypertension is a vascular disorder; renal and cardiac complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Myofibrillar degeneration defines skeletal myopathy. Cardiac involvement varies by subtype without an established umbrella frequency of at least 30%; respiratory muscle disease remains muscular.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment and frequent epileptic encephalopathy define this syndrome; other organ abnormalities lack qualifying frequencies.
Acid-base disorders belong to the metabolic axis; an underlying renal or pulmonary cause is not established by this umbrella concept.
Congenital underdevelopment of bronchi, alveoli and lung tissue directly reduces pulmonary capacity.
Malignancy of hematopoietic cells in marrow and blood; splenic involvement shares this axis. Other organ infiltration is not consistently common across leukemia subtypes.
Idiopathic catatonia is a psychiatric psychomotor syndrome; its behavioral and motor manifestations do not establish direct structural organ damage.
Benign papillomas of the vulvar vestibule arise in reproductive mucosa, outside the defined axes.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the urethra; urinary tract location determines the axis.
Syndromic intellectual disability and epilepsy directly define nervous system involvement.
Developmental abnormalities of bone and cartilage define this skeletal umbrella; extraskeletal disease is subtype dependent.
Unilateral absence or hypoplasia of the femur is a structural skeletal defect.
Defective von Willebrand factor binding to factor VIII causes an inherited coagulation disorder.
Absent thumb in 1/1 assessed; cleft hard palate and congenital cardiac defects each in 1/3. These meet the supplied threshold, but very small samples limit certainty.
A corpus luteum cyst is a reproductive ovarian lesion; an endocrine disorder is not established.
Retinal and macular dystrophy causes progressive central visual loss; the frequent findings remain within the ocular axis.
Vibration-triggered mast-cell-mediated urticaria and angioedema define a cutaneous immune-mediated disorder; transient swelling does not establish other organ damage.
A sleep-wake disorder affecting initiation and maintenance of sleep is assigned to nervous system sleep regulation; no additional organ damage is established.
Inherited skin fragility causes palmoplantar blistering. Frequent paresthesias and acute neuropathic symptoms do not establish nerve damage; oral lesions occur below 30%.
Developmental impairment and musculoskeletal defects define the syndrome; joint hypermobility affects 17/32. Strabismus and seizures each affect fewer than 30%.
Skeletal defects and intellectual impairment define the syndrome. Urinary tract anomalies and lung hypoplasia each occur in 30-79%; cap omits cleft palate (30-79%).
Macular degeneration directly damages the retina; the associated gene does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Craniofacial skeletal and ear defects define the syndrome. Limbal dermoids occur in 11/18 and developmental delay in 3/8; cap omits transverse facial clefts (3/8).
